newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: SOCCER-KABILA GOVERNMENT CHANGES NATIONAL TEAM'S NAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KABILA GOVERNMENT CHANGES NATIONAL TEAM'S NAME.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of Congo, former Zaire, has changed the name of its national soccer team from the Leopards to the Simbas -- Swahili for the Lions.
State radio and television announced the name change on Wednesday, on the eve of the inauguration of Laurent Kabila as president of Africa's third largest country.

The old name was closely associated with dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, deposed by Kabila's forces who entered the capital Kinshasa on May 17. Mobutu, who ruled for more than three decades, wore a trade-mark leopard-skin hat.
The Simbas are due to play neighbouring Congo -- the smaller Republic of Congo that is -- in a World Cup qualifier on June 8.
